response.justification: Strong, broad senior engineer with genuine geospatial domain exposure (GISCollective, Green Map web GIS) and real low-latency systems work (D-based microservices at Sociomantic handling millions of req/s with async I/O, fibers, caching). However, the core requirement — modern C++ or Rust in commercial/OSS settings — is essentially unmet: the only C/C++ experience is ~6 months at National Instruments in 2014–2015, and there is no Rust at all. The last decade is dominated by TypeScript/Node.js/Ember full-stack work, and there is no navigation guidance, routing, or map-tiling pipeline experience. Worth a screening call only if the team will accept a systems-capable polyglot willing to ramp on C++; otherwise stronger C++/geospatial candidates should be prioritized.
strengths: Genuine geospatial/GIS product experience, including a self-founded open-source geo-data platform
Proven low-latency, high-throughput distributed services work (async I/O, fibers, caching, microservices)
Demonstrated breadth and appetite to learn across stacks, plus strong testing/TDD and DevOps/Linux discipline
concerns: Minimal and dated modern C++ experience; no Rust experience listed
No navigation, routing, or map-tiling pipeline background (no tile generation, traffic signals, or map data ingestion)
Recent 5+ years are web/full-stack TypeScript-focused, signaling drift away from systems-level engineering

key_factors.factor: Geospatial and distributed low-latency systems background
